text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on April 4 in history:
1406 - King Robert III of Scotland died at Rothesay Castle and was succeeded by James I. James was being held prisoner by the English so Robert, Duke of Albany became regent.
1581 - After circumnavigating the world, Francis Drake was knighted on board The Golden Hind at Deptford in London by Queen Elizabeth I.
1611 - Christian IV of Denmark declared war on Sweden.
1617 - John Napier, Scottish mathematician, who invented the concept of logarithms, died.
1758 - Pierre-Paul Prud'hon, French painter, born; after becoming court painter to Napoleon, he painted one of his best known works, "Portrait of the Empress Josephine".
1774 - Oliver Goldsmith, Irish playwright, poet and novelist, died; best known for his novel "The Vicar of Wakefield" and the play "She Stoops to Conquer".

1841 - William Harrison, ninth president of the United States, died. After giving one of the longest inaugural addresses, he caught pneumonia and died after only 32 days in office. He was succeeded by vice-president John Tyler.

1862 - In the American Civil War, the battle of Yorktown started when a Federal army of 45,000 under McClelland tried to approach the Confederate capital of Richmond but was stopped by an opposing force of 12,000.

1875 - Piere Monteux, U.S. conductor, born in France. Famed for his interpretation of early 20th century music, he conducted the first peformances of Stravinsky's "Rite of Spring" and Ravel's "Daphnis and Chloe".
1884 - Bolivia ceded Atacama to Chile under the Treaty of Valparaiso.
1896 - Robert Emmet Sherwood, U.S. playwright and editor, born; best known for his "Idiot's Delight" and "Abe Lincoln in Illinois" for which he won Pulitzer Prizes.

1905 - 19,000 people were killed in an earthquake which struck the province of Lahore, then part of British India. The earthquake measured 8.6 on the Richter scale and demolished the towns of Kangra and Dharmsala.
1912 - A Chinese republic was proclaimed in Tibet.
1918 - The second Battle of the Somme ended with German gains of some 60 km (40 miles) at a cost of 150,000 Germans killed or wounded and 160,000 Allied casualties.
1933 - The U.S. Navy airship Akron crashed into the sea off the coast at New Jersey during a storm with the loss of 73 lives.
1939 - Faisal II acceded to the Iraqi throne on the death of his father, King Ghazi I.
1949 - The North Atlantic Treaty setting up a mutual defence alliance was signed in Washington by the foreign ministers of the 12 participating powers.
1964 - Archbishop Makarios of Cyprus abrogated the 1959 treaty between Cyprus, Greece and Turkey.
1968 - In Memphis, Tennessee, U.S. civil rights leader Dr Martin Luther King was assassinated, sparking rioting in Memphis.
1972 - The Soviet Union refused a visa to the Swedish Academy secretary who was to deliver the Nobel Prize to Alexander Solzhenitsyn.
1975 - 155 children died when a U.S. air force transport plane carrying Vietnamese orphans crashed on take-off in Saigon.

1979 - In Pakistan, ex-president Zulfikar Ali Bhutto was hanged at Rawalpindi for conspiring to murder a political opponent. He was president from 1970 until 1977, when he was deposed by General Zia ul-Haq.
1983 - Gloria Swanson, U.S. stage and screen actress, died. Her film career began in 1913 and her most famous role was that of a faded silent movie actress in the 1950 film "Sunset Boulevard".
1990 - Britain published a controversial bill to grant citizenship to up to 225,000 Hong Kong residents in the runup to the colony's handover to China in 1997.
1995 - Moslem rebels attacked the small Philippine town of Ipil, destroying most of the town centre; 53 people were killed.
1996 - An Italian military court judge ordered former SS Captain Erich Priebke to stand trial for his role in the 1944 massacre of 335 Italian men and boys at the Ardeatine Caves outside Rome.
